Coriolis force: In physics, the Coriolis force is a pseudo-force that acts on objects in motion within a frame of reference that rotates with respect to an inertial frame.
TeX: Donald Knuth. TeX is a popular means of typesetting complex mathematical formulae; it has been noted as one of the most sophisticated digital typographical systems.
Methotrexate: Pfizer. Methotrexate, formerly known as amethopterin, is a chemotherapy agent and immune-system suppressant.
Which country is Hawker Hunter from?
Hawker Hunter: United Kingdom. The all-weather/night fighter role was filled by the Gloster Javelin.
Who is credited with discovering Bohrium?
Bohrium: Yuri Oganessian. Bohrium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bh and atomic number 107.
Who is credited with discovering 10 Hygiea?
10 Hygiea: Annibale de Gasparis. 10 Hygiea is a large asteroid in the outer region of the main asteroid belt, between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
Who is credited with discovering Nickel?
Nickel: Axel Fredrik Cronstedt. Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.
Roughly two-thirds of the 150,000 people who die each day succumb to causes linked to this gradual, damage-driven process of growing older — what is it?
Ageing (or aging in American English) is the process of becoming older.
From a Greek word meaning 'dissection,' which old branch of natural science is paired with physiology to study living things' structure and function?
Anatomy (from Ancient Greek (anatom) 'dissection') is the branch of morphology concerned with the study of the internal and external structure of organisms and their parts.

Which plant family of about 181 genera and 2,600 species, nearly all found in the tropics, includes climbers, shrubs, and tree-like forms with large fan- or feather-shaped fronds atop mostly unbranched stems?
Arecaceae are a family of perennial, flowering plants in the monocot order Arecales.

Manufactured by a Turkish company and credited largely to a former MIT graduate, this medium-altitude combat drone has become one of the most exported unmanned aircraft of its era — what aircraft (family) is it?
Baykar Bayraktar TB2 is a family of medium-altitude long-endurance (MALE) unmanned combat aerial vehicles (UCAV) capable of remotely controlled or autonomous flight operations.
A child prodigy who wrote a treatise on conic sections at 16, which Frenchman later traded letters with Fermat on probability and built early calculating machines?
Blaise Pascal (19 June 1623 - 19 August 1662) was a French mathematician, physicist, inventor, philosopher, and Catholic writer.

Naturally green and yellow with scalloped black markings, this small, long-tailed seed-eating parrot native to Australia is bred worldwide in colors from blue to white — which bird, also called a budgie?
Budgerigar (--ree-; Melopsittacus undulatus), also known as the common parakeet, shell parakeet or budgie, is a small, long-tailed, seed-eating parrot native to Australia.

Born in London and raised in Milan, this Italian Catholic teenager taught himself computer programming and web design to promote devotion to the Eucharist online before his death in 2006 at age 15 — who was he?
Carlo Acutis (3 May 1991 - 12 October 2006) was an English-born Italian Catholic teenager known for his devotion to the Eucharist and his use of digital media to promote Catholic devotion.
Often preceded by a gallbladder attack and typically caused by a gallstone lodging in the cystic duct, which condition can progress to complications like gallstone pancreatitis?
Cholecystitis is inflammation of the gallbladder. Often gallbladder attacks (biliary colic) precede acute cholecystitis.

The most widely distributed corvid, this large all-black bird is found across the Northern Hemisphere and is the heaviest passerine bird, with 11 accepted subspecies showing little variation in appearance. What bird is this?
Common raven (Corvus corax) is a large all-black passerine bird.
This transdisciplinary field studies circular causal processes like feedback and recursion, where an action's outcome becomes the input for the next — what field is it?
Cybernetics is the transdisciplinary study of circular causal processes such as feedback and recursion, where the outcomes of actions return as inputs for subsequent actions.
Domesticated over 14,000 years ago — before farming even began — this descendant of wolves shares a common ancestor with the modern gray wolf. What animal is it?
Dog (Canis familiaris or Canis lupus familiaris) is a domesticated descendant of wolves.
This is the earliest developmental stage of a multicellular organism, beginning with a single-celled zygote formed just after fertilization — what is it called?
Embryo is the initial stage of development for a multicellular organism.
Known for thin, tapered wings built for high-speed flight and rapid turns, this genus of roughly 40 raptor species includes types called hobbies and kestrels — what are they?
Falcon are birds of prey in the genus Falco, which includes about 40 species.
After working in Feynman's group on the Manhattan Project, this physicist later co-detected a famously elusive elementary particle, winning the 1995 Nobel — who was he?
Frederick Reines (March 16, 1918 - August 26, 1998) was an American physicist.
The simplest stable amino acid, with just a single hydrogen for a side chain, it's the only common one that isn't chiral and makes up about 35% of collagen — what is it?
Glycine (symbol Gly or G) is an organic compound with the formula C2H5NO2, and is the simplest stable amino acid, distinguished by having a single hydrogen atom as its side chain.
This wingless insect spends its entire life on the human scalp, feeds only on blood, and has legs too short and stumpy to jump or even walk well on a flat surface — what is it?
Head louse (Pediculus humanus capitis) is an obligate ectoparasite of humans.
Native to Japan, this deciduous shrub grows big flower heads that can turn pink or blue and is also known as the mophead or lacecap — which plant?
Hydrangea macrophylla is a species of flowering plant in the family Hydrangeaceae, native and endemic to Japan.
Lasting anywhere from a few days to over a month, this disorder makes it hard to fall or stay asleep, leaving daytime drowsiness, irritability and trouble focusing in its wake — what is it?
Insomnia is a sleep disorder causing difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep for as long as desired.
This English scientist's 1808 book proposed that elements consist of identical atoms combining in fixed whole-number ratios, laying the groundwork for modern atomic theory — who is he?
John Dalton (5 or 6 September 1766 - 27 July 1844) was an English chemist, physicist, and meteorologist whose work laid the foundations of modern atomic theory and stoichiometric chemistry.
Despite being a kingfisher, this Australian bird rarely goes near water and can grow up to about 47 centimeters long — what is it?
Kookaburra are terrestrial tree kingfishers of the genus Dacelo native to Australia and New Guinea, which grow to between 28 and 47 cm (11 and 19 in) in length and weigh around 300 g (11 oz).

First isolated from linseed oil and named from the Latin words for 'flax' and 'oil,' this omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acid is one of the two essential fats humans must get from their diet — which acid?
Linoleic acid (LA) is an organic compound with the formula CH3(CH2)4CH=CHCH2CH=CH(CH2)7COOH.

A chemical element with symbol Mg and atomic number 12, it's a shiny gray metal with low density and high chemical reactivity that readily reacts with air to form a thin passivation oxide coating. What element is this?
Magnesium is a chemical element; it has symbol Mg and atomic number 12. The free metal burns with a brilliant-white light.
First isolated from a cow's pineal gland in 1958 because it could lighten the skin of frogs, this nighttime hormone went on to become famous for governing the sleep-wake cycle — what is it?
Melatonin is a natural compound produced by various organisms, including bacteria and eukaryotes.
With over 86,000 living species spanning sea, freshwater, and even land, this is the largest of all marine phyla — what is it?
Mollusca is a phylum of protostomic invertebrate animals, whose members are known as molluscs or mollusks.

What term, coined in the mid-19th century and often attributed to pathologist Rudolf Virchow, describes the premature death of cells in living tissue due to external injury or infection, as opposed to programmed cell death?
Necrosis (from Ancient Greek (nkrsis) 'death') is a form of cell injury which results in the premature death of cells in living tissue by autolysis.
Despite the zebra-like stripes on its legs, this shy mammal of the northeastern Congo is actually the giraffe's only living cousin — and the sole other member of the family Giraffidae. What is it?
Okapi (Okapia johnstoni), also known as the forest giraffe, and zebra giraffe, is an artiodactyl mammal that is endemic to the northeast Democratic Republic of the Congo in central Africa.

This inflammation of the skin around the nail is often triggered by frequent hand washing or cuticle trauma like nail biting, and is treated with antibiotics or antifungals depending on the cause — what condition is it?
Paronychia is an inflammation of the skin around the nail, often due to bacteria or fungi.

Associated with the early 20th century, this philosophical movement tries to objectively describe subjective conscious experience exactly as it appears, without assuming anything about the outside world — which movement?
Phenomenology (philosophy) is a philosophical study and movement largely associated with the early 20th century that seeks to objectively investigate the nature of subjective, conscious experience.

It plays out everywhere from the clans of traditional societies up through modern governments, and its practitioners negotiate, make laws, and sometimes wage war; what is this activity of settling a society's affairs?
Politics is the activity of settling affairs in an organized society. Politics is usually concerned with resolving issues within a society via a government.
Its biological practitioners link it to neuroscience while its social scientists study groups, all in service of studying the mind and behavior — what is this academic discipline?
Psychology is the scientific study of the mind and behavior. Psychology is an academic discipline of broad scope, crossing the boundaries between the natural and social sciences.

This genus of roughly 60 herbaceous perennials in the buckwheat family includes the familiar pie vegetable prized for its tart stalks despite mildly toxic leaves — which genus, native to Europe and Asia?
Rheum (plant) is a genus of about 60 herbaceous perennial plants in the family Polygonaceae.
This grayish-leaved, purple-flowered evergreen subshrub is a Mediterranean member of the mint family, long used both as a culinary herb and an ornamental garden plant — what plant is it?
Salvia officinalis is a perennial, evergreen subshrub, with woody stems, grayish leaves, and blue to purplish flowers.
Before becoming the first woman on Facebook's board, this executive ran global sales at Google and assisted Lawrence Summers at the World Bank — who later wrote 'Lean In'?
Sheryl Sandberg (born August 28, 1969) is an American technology executive, philanthropist and writer.
Usually diagnosed in infancy, this rare genetic disorder caused by a mutation in the SMN1 gene is the leading inherited cause of death in babies if left untreated — what condition is it?
Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a rare neuromuscular disorder that results in the loss of motor neurons and progressive muscle wasting.

In the nervous system, this structure lets one neuron send or receive signals with a neighboring cell, and comes in both chemical and electrical varieties — the electrical kind linked directly through gap junctions — name this structure?
Synapse is a structure that allows a neuron to exchange (receive or send) signals with another cell in its immediate vicinity.

When a piece of this obstruction breaks free and travels through the body it's called an embolus, and it can trigger a stroke or heart attack — what is the formation of a blood clot inside a vessel called?
Thrombosis (from Ancient Greek (thrmbsis) 'clotting') is the formation of a blood clot inside a blood vessel, obstructing the flow of blood through the circulatory system.

This flowering plant in the ginger family is native to the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia, requiring temperatures between 68 and 86°F and high rainfall. Its rhizomes are gathered and can be used fresh or dried for consumption and dyeing — what is it?
Turmeric is a flowering plant in the ginger family Zingiberaceae. Turmeric powder has a warm, bitter, black pepper-like flavor and earthy, mustard-like aroma.
One of the oldest leaf vegetables eaten by humans, this fast-growing aquatic plant in the cabbage family shares its peppery bite with relatives like mustard, radish, and wasabi — what plant is it?
Watercress (Nasturtium officinale) is a species of aquatic flowering plant in the cabbage family, Brassicaceae.
Earning his doctorate in Islamic philosophy at George Washington University under Seyyed Hossein Nasr, this Turkish academic now directs the country's National Intelligence Organization — who is he?
İbrahim Kalın (born 15 September 1971) is a Turkish bureaucrat and academic who is the current director of the National Intelligence Organization (MT).
Considered sacred by Hindus and Buddhists, this tree native to the Indian subcontinent is also known as bael and is the sole member of its genus — which species?
Aegle marmelos: Species of tree, considered sacred by Hindus. It is present in India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and Nepal as a naturalized species.
With the general formula CnH2n+2 and every carbon-carbon bond single, methane is the simplest example of this class of hydrocarbons — what's it called?
Alkane: Type of saturated hydrocarbon compound.
This group of diseases occurs when misfolded proteins accumulate in body tissue, causing fatigue, swelling, and shortness of breath among roughly 36 distinct protein-driven types — what is it?
Amyloidosis: Metabolic disease involving abnormal deposited amyloid proteins.
When an injury to the wall of the body's main artery lets blood force its layers apart, victims often feel a sudden 'tearing' chest or back pain — what's this medical emergency called?
Aortic dissection: Injury to the innermost layer of the aorta.

With the symbol At and atomic number 85, this is the rarest naturally occurring element in Earth's crust, so radioactive that a macroscopic sample would instantly vaporize itself — what element is it?
Astatine: Chemical element with atomic number 85 (At). It is the rarest naturally occurring element in the Earth's crust, occurring only as the decay product of various heavier elements.
A sessile marine arthropod related to crabs and lobsters, folklore once claimed geese hatched fully formed from one variety of it — what creature is it?
Barnacle: Subclass of sessile marine crustaceans.
This natural science rests on five big themes — the cell, genes and heredity, evolution, energy transformation, and homeostasis — to explain life itself. What field is it?

Despite lacking the tight head of typical cabbage, this leafy Chinese vegetable has a flavor often compared to spinach and water chestnuts, with a milder white bulb and stronger-tasting green leaves — what vegetable is it?
Bok choy: Subspecies of flowering plant.
With a large head, deep facial folds, and a flat face with a jutting lower jaw, this British breed's ancestors were once used for baiting cattle before the sport was banned in 1835 — which breed?
Bulldog: British breed of dog. It may also be known as the English Bulldog or British Bulldog.
This Sicilian pastry is a fried, tube-shaped shell filled with sweet ricotta, dressed up with candied orange zest in Palermo or chopped pistachios in Catania — what treat is it?
Cannoli: Italian ricotta-filled pastry. Cannoli are Sicilian pastries consisting of a tube-shaped shell of fried pastry dough, filled with a sweet and creamy filling containing ricotta cheese.
Native to the western Himalayas and the Mediterranean's high altitudes, this coniferous genus bears erect cones and wood that naturally repels moths — which genus?
Found across North America (and one Siberian species in Asia), these small striped squirrels stash food in their cheek pouches to store for winter — what are they?
Also known as a trefoil for its three-part leaves, this legume has been farmed for over 1,000 years to fix nitrogen in soil, and a rare four-leaf version is considered a good-luck charm — what plant?
This medium-to-large sea snail's shell tapers to a noticeable point at both ends thanks to its high spire and siphonal canal — what type of shelled creature is it?
Conch: Shell or sea snails. Conch (US: KONK, KONCH, UK: KONCH) is any of a number of different medium-to-large-sized sea snails.
This practice of secure communication sits at the intersection of math, computer science, and electrical engineering, and underpins e-commerce and chip-based payment cards — what is it called?
Cryptography: Practice and study of secure communication techniques.
From muntjac to moose, members of the family Cervidae shed and regrow bony skull extensions each year — antlers used to battle rivals. What hoofed ruminant is this?
Deer: Family of hoofed mammals. A deer (pl.: deer) or true deer is a hoofed ruminant ungulate of the family Cervidae (informally the deer family).
Bred around 1890 by a Thuringian tax collector looking for a loyal guard dog, this sleek, high-alert German breed traditionally had its ears cropped and tail docked — which breed?
Dobermann: Black and tan dog breed from Germany.
After stints at the CIA, Dell, and Booz Allen Hamilton, this NSA contractor flew to Hong Kong in 2013 and leaked thousands of classified documents exposing global surveillance — who is he?
Edward Snowden: Whistleblower and NSA contractor (born 1983)
One of the four basic animal tissue types, this thin protective cell layer lines blood vessels and body cavities and includes the skin's outer layer — what is it called?
Epithelium: Tissue lining the surfaces of organs in animals.
In this small bird of prey, females can be up to 25% larger than males — one of the biggest size gaps between sexes of any bird — and it hunts garden songbirds across Europe and Asia — which raptor?

Eurasian sparrowhawk: Species of bird. The Eurasian sparrowhawk (Accipiter nisus), also known as the northern sparrowhawk or simply the sparrowhawk, is a small bird of prey in the family Accipitridae.
Marketed under brand names like Allegra, this second-generation antihistamine treats allergy symptoms without crossing the blood-brain barrier the way older drugs do — what medication is it?
Fexofenadine: Antihistamine medication. Fexofenadine is an antihistamine medication used in the treatment of allergy symptoms such as allergic rhinitis and urticaria.
Dead at just 26, this British thinker had already reshaped philosophy, mathematics and economics — and as an undergraduate translated Wittgenstein's 'Tractatus' into English; who was he?
Frank P. Ramsey: British philosopher, mathematician and economist (1903–1930)
With a siphon that can stretch over three feet and a shell just 6 to 8 inches across, this giant Pacific burrowing clam can live up to 179 years — which creature?
This waterfowl family member is smaller than a swan but larger than a duck; its young are called goslings, and a flock on the ground is known as a gaggle — what bird is it?
Goose: Common name for a group of waterfowl.
Producing up to a hundred billion new cells a day from specialized stem cells, this biological process manufactures every component of blood — what is it?
Haematopoiesis: Formation of blood cellular components.
Introduced to Britain in the 19th century as an ornamental plant, this Caucasus-native's sap causes painful blistering burns when exposed skin meets sunlight — which species?
Heracleum mantegazzianum: Species of flowering plant. Heracleum mantegazzianum, commonly known as giant hogweed, is a monocarpic perennial herbaceous plant in the carrot family Apiaceae.

In the Renaissance this field of study covered classical literature and language rather than religion or divinity, and today it groups subjects using critical and interpretive methods rather than empirical ones — what broad academic category is this?
Humanities: Academic disciplines that study society and culture.
This Russian-American engineer built the first successful four-engine aircraft in 1913 and went on to pioneer the modern helicopter — who was he?
A self-taught rocketeer and practicing occultist, this co-founder of both JPL and Aerojet invented the first castable composite rocket propellant before dying young in 1952. Who was he?
This English mathematician dreamed up the cellular automaton known as the Game of Life and spent his later years at Princeton — who was he?
Derived from Greek words for 'movement' and 'study,' this scientific field examines biomechanics, motor control, and rehabilitation to understand how the human body moves — what field is this?
Kinesiology: Study of human body movement. Kinesiology addresses physiological, anatomical, biomechanical, pathological, neuropsychological principles and mechanisms of movement.
This genus of bacteria mainly infects amoebae but can cause a pneumonia-like illness in humans when it spreads via poorly maintained cooling towers — what genus is it?
Legionella: Pathogenic genus of Gram-negative bacteria.

This catch-all name covers over 7,000 squamate species on every continent but Antarctica — from finger-length geckos to the three-meter Komodo dragon, with a few 'legless' lineages thrown in. What is it?
Found from Gibraltar to across Asia, these Old World monkeys live in troops centered on dominant matriarchs, and one Malaysian species eats about 70 rats a year — what are they?
Macaque: Genus of Old World monkeys. The macaques constitute a genus (Macaca) of gregarious Old World monkeys of the subfamily Cercopithecinae.
Prized by fur trappers for its yellowish-to-dark-brown coat, this bushy-tailed, weasel-like mammal is adapted to life in the taiga's coniferous forests — what is it?

Diagnosed when a person has at least three of five red flags -- including abdominal obesity and high blood pressure -- this cluster of conditions raises the risk of heart disease and diabetes in about a quarter of US adults. What is it?
Metabolic syndrome: Cluster of diseases occurring with obesity.
Marketed under names like Rogaine and Loniten, this medication treats high blood pressure but is best known over-the-counter for combating hair loss — what's the drug?
Minoxidil: Medication to treat high blood pressure and alopecia.
Nicknamed the barking deer for its unusual call, this small Asian deer genus has fossils dating back as far as 35 million years — what is it?
This general term describes inflammation of the kidneys, affecting structures such as the glomeruli, tubules, or the surrounding interstitial tissue — what is the condition called?
Nephritis: Inflammation of the kidneys. It is one of several different types of nephropathy.
The largest structure inside a eukaryotic cell's nucleus, this site of ribosome assembly also helps form signal recognition particles and responds to cellular stress — what is it?
Nucleolus: Largest structure in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells. The nucleolus also participates in the formation of signal recognition particles and plays a role in the cell's response to stress.

Believed to be the world's fourth-leading cause of disability, this degenerative joint disease comes from the breakdown of cartilage and bone, often striking the fingertips, thumb base, knees, and hips — what is it?
Osteoarthritis: Form of arthritis caused by degeneration of joints.

Also called the blue passionflower, this South American vine climbs via tendrils to 10 metres, bears fragrant blue-white blooms with a fringed coronal filament, and produces an edible but not particularly tasty orange fruit — which plant is it?
Passiflora caerulea: Species of flowering plant in the passion flower family.

Positioned behind the mouth and nasal cavity, this throat structure channels food toward the esophagus and air toward the larynx, with a flap of cartilage guarding against the two crossing paths — what is it?
Pharynx: Part of the throat that is behind the mouth and nasal cavity.

Derived in 1900 by a German physicist who proposed that an oscillator's energy could only change in discrete increments, this principle describes the spectral density of radiation from a black body at a given temperature — what is it called?
Planck's law: Spectral density of light emitted by a black body.
This common name describes small aquatic crustaceans with an exoskeleton and ten legs, especially popular in the UK and Commonwealth nations for larger swimming decapods — what is it?
Prawn: Common name applied to some types of crustaceans.
This seabird's large, colorful beak fades after breeding season, and its short wings beat up to 400 times a minute to keep it airborne — what bird is it?
Domesticated roughly 8,000 years ago, this Southeast Asian bird species is the primary wild ancestor of today's chickens — which bird?
Red junglefowl: Species of bird; ancestor of the chicken. The red junglefowl was the primary species to give rise to today's many breeds of chicken (G. g. domesticus).
Nicknamed the 'Bone,' this variable-sweep-wing heavy bomber was dreamed up to fuse the B-58's Mach 2 speed with the B-52's range and payload — which aircraft is it?
Rockwell B-1 Lancer: American strategic bomber.
Commonly known as elder, with its blossoms called elderflower and its fruit elderberry, this genus contains between 20 and 30 flowering plant species — which genus?
The sole living species in its genus, this coastal California evergreen is the tallest tree species on Earth, reaching over 116 meters and living 2,200 years or more. What is it?
Sequoia sempervirens: Species of tree. Sequoia sempervirens is the sole living species of the genus Sequoia in the cypress family Cupressaceae (formerly treated in Taxodiaceae).

Named in 1842 from Brazilian fossils and often called a saber-toothed tiger despite no close kinship to true tigers, this genus of prehistoric predator roamed the Americas until the early Holocene — which animal?
Smilodon: Extinct genus of saber-toothed cat.
With eight arms plus two extra tentacles for grabbing prey, this soft-bodied mollusc has an internal chitin rod called a gladius instead of a true skeleton — what creature is it?

A retired US Navy captain, this NASA astronaut became the first woman to fly on an orbital spacecraft's test flight in 2024 and had her ISS stay extended by more than nine months due to technical issues — who is she?
Sunita Williams: U.S. Navy officer and NASA astronaut (born 1965)
A math prodigy who abandoned academia in 1969 for a reclusive cabin life, the 'Unabomber' mailed bombs for 17 years and published a 35,000-word anti-technology manifesto — who was he?
Shaped like a butterfly and sitting in the neck just below the Adam's apple, this endocrine gland secretes hormones that regulate metabolic rate — which gland is it?
Thyroid: Endocrine gland in the neck. The lower two thirds of the lobes are connected by a thin band of tissue called the isthmus (pl.: isthmi).
This ester of glycerol and three fatty acids is the main constituent of body fat and a major component of human skin oils — what is it?
Triglyceride: Any ester of glycerol having all three hydroxyl groups esterified with fatty acids.
Before becoming the first woman in space aboard a solo 1963 flight that orbited Earth 48 times, this cosmonaut worked in a textile factory and skydove as a hobby — who is she?
Valentina Tereshkova: Russian cosmonaut and politician (born 1937)
Denoted by the Greek letter lambda, this measure of a repeating wave's spatial period shrinks as frequency rises for a wave moving at constant speed — what is it called?
Wavelength: Distance over which a wave's shape repeats.
Spread mainly by the oriental rat flea, this gram-negative bacterium caused the Black Death and the Plague of Justinian — what is it?
Yersinia pestis: Species of bacteria, cause of plague.

The symbol for livermorium is Lv. Livermorium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lv and atomic number 116.
